pitfalls: list.sort() mutates and returns None. sorted() returns a new list.
Repeated references share mutations. Construct each row separately.
Zero is false in a boolean condition. Use explicit sentinels.
/ produces a floating result. // floors, including negatives. −7 // 3 is −3; truncation toward zero gives −2.
List and string slices allocate new sequences. Account for their time and memory.
Do not add/delete keys from a dict/set while iterating it. Iterate a snapshot or collect changes first.
A default list is created once, not on every call. Use None then create a list.
Check bounds or emptiness before indexing or popping. and/or evaluate left to right.

if stack and stack[-1] == target:
    stack.pop()
a=b=[] shares a list. Tuple assignment evaluates all right-hand values first.

a, b = [], []
left, right = right, left
Set elements and dict keys must be hashable. Use a tuple rather than a list for a coordinate.
Counter counts items. defaultdict creates values for missing keys; reading a missing key can insert it.
Deep DFS may hit Python recursion limits. Use an iterative stack for very deep chains.
list membership is linear; set/dict membership is expected constant time. pop(0) shifts a list; deque.popleft does not.
Match the supplied function name, parameters and return type. Do not print instead of returning. Check whether stdin/stdout is required.
